page: Vultr vhf-1c-1gb is an entry-level virtual machine within the High Frequency Compute series. The instance runs on an x86_64 Intel processor configured with 1 shared vCPU (1 physical core and 1 thread) operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor cache configuration provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with instruction set support including AVX, AES-NI, BMI2, and FMA. Memory capacity is fixed at 1.0 GB of RAM. The instance includes 32 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and comes provisioned with 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate adequate performance in isolated single-threaded compute tasks, contrasting with low overall throughput due to its single-thread and single-vCPU ceiling. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU throughput reached 1865.79, placing it in the middle 50% tier, while multi-core scoring remained identical due to the single-core constraint, placing it in the bottom 10%. Memory throughput reflects hardware limits, showing 16.75 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 13.63 GB/sec for large-block writes. Compression tasks showed average performance, with single-threaded gzip registering 28.26 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 9.41 GB/sec. Conversely, overall PassMark metrics placed the instance in the bottom decile, recording a 2239.98 CPU score, 974.54 memory score, and 1027.68 for database operations.

The qualitative trade-off of the vhf-1c-1gb lies between its responsive NVMe local storage and its constrained compute and memory footprint. With a 1:1 ratio of vCPU to gigabytes of RAM and shared CPU scheduling, the system offers entry-level resource access suitable for light background processes, small static web endpoints, or configuration testing. It is constrained for multi-threaded applications, large memory-resident datasets, or production database servers.
description: Vultr vhf-1c-1gb is a budget-tier virtual instance within the High Frequency Compute line, featuring 1 shared Intel x86_64 vCPU operating at 2.0 GHz, 1.0 GB of RAM, and 32 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The single-core configuration achieves moderate single-threaded performance, recording 1865.79 in stress-ng single-core tests and 28.26 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. However, overall throughput is constrained by the shared single-core limitation and 1.0 GB memory footprint, reflected in bottom-decile PassMark CPU (2239.98) and memory (974.54) scores. With 1 bundled public IPv4 address and local NVMe storage, this instance is suited for lightweight utility services, single-threaded batch scripts, or low-traffic static web hosting.
